00:47:09,520 --> 00:47:11,460
going to connect it that way.

939
00:47:11,460 --> 00:47:13,620
CHRISTOPHER COTTEN- Trees will not preserve connections.

940
00:47:13,620 --> 00:47:15,120
That's just the name of the game.

941
00:47:15,120 --> 00:47:16,700
We have to allow this.

942
00:47:16,700 --> 00:47:18,100
Otherwise, we can't do anything.

943
00:47:18,100 --> 00:47:19,760
That's the short version.

944
00:47:19,760 --> 00:47:21,200
OK?

945
00:47:21,200 --> 00:47:21,700
OK.

946
00:47:21,700 --> 00:47:24,720
In the last few minutes, let me talk about how we take these

947
00:47:24,720 --> 00:47:26,820
trees and implement a solution.

948
00:47:26,820 --> 00:47:28,880
A set or sequence.

949
00:47:28,880 --> 00:47:29,380
OK?

950
00:47:29,380 --> 00:47:30,680
I've already alluded to this.

951
00:47:34,980 --> 00:47:44,800
So for a sequence, we just make the traversal order

952
00:47:44,800 --> 00:47:49,420
equal to the order that we're trying to represent,

953
00:47:49,420 --> 00:47:50,260
the sequence order.

954
00:47:53,700 --> 00:47:56,380
And if we're trying to sort a set of items with keys,

955
00:47:56,380 --> 00:48:02,300
we're going to make the traversal order equal to,

956
00:48:02,300 --> 00:48:05,000
ordered by increasing key.

957
00:48:05,000 --> 00:48:08,820
Increasing item key.

958
00:48:13,320 --> 00:48:14,820
In some sense, that's it.

959
00:48:14,820 --> 00:48:17,320
But then we need to think about how do we implement

960
00:48:17,320 --> 00:48:19,060
all of these operations.

961
00:48:19,060 --> 00:48:23,260
So maybe most enlightening is, for starters,

962
00:48:23,260 --> 00:48:26,300
is finding a key in a tree.

963
00:48:26,380 --> 00:48:31,740
So this is going to correspond to binary search.

964
00:48:31,740 --> 00:48:36,600
If I'm searching for a key, let's say I'm searching for G's

965
00:48:36,600 --> 00:48:41,000
key, and I know, this may be hard in this example,

966
00:48:41,000 --> 00:48:43,840
maybe I'll replace these all with numbers

967
00:48:43,840 --> 00:48:48,820
so I can think about key values.

968
00:48:48,820 --> 00:48:49,320
OK.

969
00:48:49,320 --> 00:48:54,540
So let's say 1, 7, 12, 17, 19, and 25.

970
00:48:54,540 --> 00:48:55,040
OK.

971
00:48:55,040 --> 00:48:55,540
So I'm going to do this.

972
00:48:55,540 --> 00:48:56,060
I'm going to do this.

973
00:48:56,060 --> 00:48:58,560
1, 7, 12, 17, 19, and 25.

974
00:48:58,560 --> 00:49:01,000
This is now in key order.

975
00:49:01,000 --> 00:49:02,500
If you think of the traversal order,

976
00:49:02,500 --> 00:49:04,799
the property is that all the keys

977
00:49:04,799 --> 00:49:07,500
in the left subtree of the root are less than the root,

978
00:49:07,500 --> 00:49:10,000
and the root is less than all the keys in the right subtree,

979
00:49:10,000 --> 00:49:11,779
and recursively all the way down.

980
00:49:11,779 --> 00:49:17,680
This is something called the binary search tree property,

981
00:49:17,680 --> 00:49:20,080
BST property.

982
00:49:20,080 --> 00:49:23,540
Here we're calling them binary tree sets,

983
00:49:23,540 --> 00:49:25,220
or set binary trees.

984
00:49:25,220 --> 00:49:26,879
But they're also known in the literature

985
00:49:26,879 --> 00:49:29,500
as binary search trees, a term you may have heard before.

986
00:49:29,500 --> 00:49:30,859
So this is a special case of what

987
00:49:30,859 --> 00:49:33,600
we're doing where we're storing the keys in order.

988
00:49:33,600 --> 00:49:37,919
And then if I want to search for a key like 13,

989
00:49:37,919 --> 00:49:39,819
I compare that key with the root.

990
00:49:39,819 --> 00:49:43,100
I see, oh, it's not equal, and it's to the left

991
00:49:43,100 --> 00:49:44,799
because it's less than 17.

992
00:49:44,799 --> 00:49:46,919
So 13 is left of here.

993
00:49:46,919 --> 00:49:48,700
13 is right of 7.

994
00:49:48,700 --> 00:49:50,359
13 is right of 12.

995
00:49:50,359 --> 00:49:55,060
And so I know that this is where 13 would belong, but there's no

996
00:49:55,060 --> 00:49:55,740
right child there.

997
00:49:55,740 --> 00:49:58,740
And so I know in find, I just return nothing.

998
00:49:58,740 --> 00:50:03,640
If I was doing find previous, I would return this node

999
00:50:03,640 --> 00:50:05,920
because I have tried to go to the right.

1000
00:50:05,920 --> 00:50:08,360
The last time before I fell off the tree,

1001
00:50:08,360 --> 00:50:09,740
I was trying to go to the right.

1002
00:50:09,740 --> 00:50:12,860
And therefore, that last node I had was the previous item.

1003
00:50:12,860 --> 00:50:15,340
If I was trying to do find next, what would I do?

1004
00:50:15,340 --> 00:50:18,600
I would just take this node and compute its successor, which

1005
00:50:18,600 --> 00:50:19,860
we already know how to do.

1006
00:50:19,860 --> 00:50:22,120
And that happens to be the root.

1007
00:50:22,120 --> 00:50:24,640
So now I can do these inexact searches.

1008
00:50:24,640 --> 00:50:27,940
When I do find previous and find next, when I fall off the tree,

1009
00:50:27,940 --> 00:50:30,020
I find either the previous or the next.

1010
00:50:30,020 --> 00:50:31,680
And then with predecessor or successor,

1011
00:50:31,680 --> 00:50:33,420
I can find the other one.

1012
00:50:33,420 --> 00:50:41,100
So that's how we can do find and find previous and find next.

1013
00:50:41,100 --> 00:50:47,240
To do sequences, we need a little bit more work.

1014
00:50:47,240 --> 00:50:50,200
We'll do that next time.

1015
00:50:54,640 --> 00:50:55,640
Thank you.

And if I get to the leaf, I'm done.

857
00:43:24,940 --> 00:43:26,800
So I'm not quite done because this is not a leaf.

858
00:43:26,800 --> 00:43:27,300
So again.

859
00:43:27,300 --> 00:43:28,500
I look at a's predecessor.

860
00:43:28,500 --> 00:43:29,720
It's now g.

861
00:43:29,720 --> 00:43:37,100
Predecessor, we hope, is always farther down in the tree.

862
00:43:37,100 --> 00:43:38,940
And then I swap a with g.

863
00:43:42,820 --> 00:43:46,980
I have preserved the traversal order except where a falls,

864
00:43:46,980 --> 00:43:49,500
just by moving a earlier in the order here.

865
00:43:49,500 --> 00:43:51,840
And now a is a leaf, and I can erase it.

866
00:43:54,720 --> 00:43:56,700
So that's what we're going to follow.

867
00:43:56,700 --> 00:43:57,200
Now.

868
00:43:57,300 --> 00:43:58,680
Actuality, it's a little tricky.

869
00:43:58,680 --> 00:44:00,380
Sometimes we need to use predecessors.

870
00:44:00,380 --> 00:44:04,540
Sometimes we need to use successor.

871
00:44:04,540 --> 00:44:08,700
So the cases are if the node is a leaf,

872
00:44:08,700 --> 00:44:11,760
just detach it from the parent.

873
00:44:11,760 --> 00:44:14,260
Easy.

874
00:44:14,260 --> 00:44:16,560
That's sort of our base case in the recursion.

875
00:44:16,560 --> 00:44:22,220
Otherwise, there are two cases.

[range 3501-4060 of 4060 lines]
876
00:44:22,220 --> 00:44:26,140
So if we're not a leaf, that means we have a left child

877
00:44:26,140 --> 00:44:27,300
or a right child or both.

878
00:44:27,300 --> 00:44:29,760
Both is going to be the easy case.

879
00:44:29,760 --> 00:44:33,620
But in general, I have either there's a left child

880
00:44:33,620 --> 00:44:36,080
or there's a right child.

881
00:44:36,080 --> 00:44:37,800
In either case, I'm going to be happy.

882
00:44:37,800 --> 00:44:39,120
So I don't need a both case.

883
00:44:41,940 --> 00:44:43,680
So what do I do?

884
00:44:43,680 --> 00:44:47,160
If I have a left child, that guarantees to me

885
00:44:47,160 --> 00:44:50,540
that the node's predecessor is inside that left subtree, which

886
00:44:50,540 --> 00:44:52,900
means it's lower in the tree.

887
00:44:52,900 --> 00:44:54,900
If I didn't have a left child, the predecessor

888
00:44:54,900 --> 00:44:56,420
would actually be higher in the tree.

889
00:44:56,420 --> 00:44:57,300
And I don't want to go higher.

890
00:44:57,300 --> 00:45:01,720
So if I have a left child, I know the predecessor is lower.

891
00:45:01,720 --> 00:45:08,960
And so I'm going to swap my item, the contents of my node,

892
00:45:08,960 --> 00:45:11,300
with my predecessor's item.

893
00:45:19,220 --> 00:45:23,780
And then I'm going to recursively delete predecessor.

894
00:45:27,300 --> 00:45:34,520
And that's the case that we looked at in this code,

895
00:45:34,520 --> 00:45:36,960
in this example, because we always had a left child.

896
00:45:36,960 --> 00:45:38,840
If we have a right child but no left child,

897
00:45:38,840 --> 00:45:39,800
we just do the reverse.

898
00:45:39,800 --> 00:45:41,980
We swap with our successor's item

899
00:45:41,980 --> 00:45:43,760
and then delete the successor.

900
00:45:43,760 --> 00:45:45,620
In either case, we're going down.

901
00:45:45,620 --> 00:45:48,480
And so if we start at some node, like the root,

902
00:45:48,480 --> 00:45:52,420
every time we do this operation, we're walking down.

903
00:45:52,420 --> 00:45:53,860
And then we're walking down.

904
00:45:53,860 --> 00:45:55,600
And in general, we'll keep walking down,

905
00:45:55,600 --> 00:45:57,140
resuming where we left off, which means, oh, we're going to go down.

906
00:45:57,140 --> 00:45:59,200
And that means total amount of time we spend

907
00:45:59,200 --> 00:46:03,140
is proportional to the height of the tree, in the worst case.

908
00:46:03,140 --> 00:46:03,640
Question?

909
00:46:03,640 --> 00:46:05,640
Why isn't the ?

910
00:46:05,640 --> 00:46:10,640
Because we end up with like, now he has a right child.

911
00:46:10,640 --> 00:46:15,140
You see, but he never had a right child.

912
00:46:15,140 --> 00:46:16,140
JOHN MCCUTCHAN- Right.

913
00:46:16,140 --> 00:46:17,759
So he didn't used to have a right child.

914
00:46:17,759 --> 00:46:19,359
So we're changing identities of nodes

915
00:46:19,359 --> 00:46:23,080
when we do this, because we didn't actually

916
00:46:23,080 --> 00:46:24,259
move this circle.

917
00:46:24,259 --> 00:46:25,420
The circle stayed in place.

918
00:46:25,420 --> 00:46:26,960
And what we changed was the item that

919
00:46:26,960 --> 00:46:28,720
was stored in that circle.

920
00:46:28,720 --> 00:46:33,200
So whether you call this node E or A, it doesn't really matter.

921
00:46:33,200 --> 00:46:35,820
It is just the root node.

922
00:46:35,820 --> 00:46:37,560
So we're going to play a lot of these tricks

923
00:46:37,560 --> 00:46:38,700
of moving the items around.

924
00:46:38,700 --> 00:46:40,100
So far, we hadn't been doing that.

925
00:46:40,100 --> 00:46:43,880
We've just been creating nodes and placing them somewhere.

926
00:46:43,880 --> 00:46:45,740
But now, in this delete operation,

927
00:46:45,740 --> 00:46:47,540
this is the first time where we're changing

928
00:46:47,540 --> 00:46:49,400
what's stored in the nodes.

929
00:46:49,400 --> 00:46:51,340
But we still can define the traversal order.

930
00:46:51,340 --> 00:46:55,780
The traversal order of this tree is D, B, G, E, H, C, which

931
00:46:55,780 --> 00:46:56,960
should be what we get here.

932
00:46:56,960 --> 00:46:59,960
If I delete F and A.

933
00:46:59,960 --> 00:47:02,960
What if you created a local tree

934
00:47:02,960 --> 00:47:04,720
and you wanted to make it different?

935
00:47:04,720 --> 00:47:05,520
Sorry, F.

936
00:47:05,520 --> 00:47:07,600
Like, it really matters to you.

937
00:47:07,600 --> 00:47:09,520
Like, it really matters to me, so you're

938
00:47:09,520 --> 00:47:11,460
going to connect it that way.

939
00:47:11,460 --> 00:47:13,620
CHRISTOPHER COTTEN- Trees will not preserve connections.

940
00:47:13,620 --> 00:47:15,120
That's just the name of the game.

941
00:47:15,120 --> 00:47:16,700
We have to allow this.

942
00:47:16,700 --> 00:47:18,100
Otherwise, we can't do anything.

943
00:47:18,100 --> 00:47:19,760
That's the short version.

944
00:47:19,760 --> 00:47:21,200
OK?

945
00:47:21,200 --> 00:47:21,700
OK.

946
00:47:21,700 --> 00:47:24,720
In the last few minutes, let me talk about how we take these

947
00:47:24,720 --> 00:47:26,820
trees and implement a solution.

948
00:47:26,820 --> 00:47:28,880
A set or sequence.

949
00:47:28,880 --> 00:47:29,380
OK?

950
00:47:29,380 --> 00:47:30,680
I've already alluded to this.

951
00:47:34,980 --> 00:47:44,800
So for a sequence, we just make the traversal order

952
00:47:44,800 --> 00:47:49,420
equal to the order that we're trying to represent,

953
00:47:49,420 --> 00:47:50,260
the sequence order.

954
00:47:53,700 --> 00:47:56,380
And if we're trying to sort a set of items with keys,

955
00:47:56,380 --> 00:48:02,300
we're going to make the traversal order equal to,

956
00:48:02,300 --> 00:48:05,000
ordered by increasing key.

957
00:48:05,000 --> 00:48:08,820
Increasing item key.

958
00:48:13,320 --> 00:48:14,820
In some sense, that's it.

959
00:48:14,820 --> 00:48:17,320
But then we need to think about how do we implement

960
00:48:17,320 --> 00:48:19,060
all of these operations.

961
00:48:19,060 --> 00:48:23,260
So maybe most enlightening is, for starters,

962
00:48:23,260 --> 00:48:26,300
is finding a key in a tree.

963
00:48:26,380 --> 00:48:31,740
So this is going to correspond to binary search.

964
00:48:31,740 --> 00:48:36,600
If I'm searching for a key, let's say I'm searching for G's

965
00:48:36,600 --> 00:48:41,000
key, and I know, this may be hard in this example,

966
00:48:41,000 --> 00:48:43,840
maybe I'll replace these all with numbers

967
00:48:43,840 --> 00:48:48,820
so I can think about key values.

968
00:48:48,820 --> 00:48:49,320
OK.

969
00:48:49,320 --> 00:48:54,540
So let's say 1, 7, 12, 17, 19, and 25.

970
00:48:54,540 --> 00:48:55,040
OK.

971
00:48:55,040 --> 00:48:55,540
So I'm going to do this.

972
00:48:55,540 --> 00:48:56,060
I'm going to do this.

973
00:48:56,060 --> 00:48:58,560
1, 7, 12, 17, 19, and 25.

974
00:48:58,560 --> 00:49:01,000
This is now in key order.

975
00:49:01,000 --> 00:49:02,500
If you think of the traversal order,

976
00:49:02,500 --> 00:49:04,799
the property is that all the keys

977
00:49:04,799 --> 00:49:07,500
in the left subtree of the root are less than the root,

978
00:49:07,500 --> 00:49:10,000
and the root is less than all the keys in the right subtree,

979
00:49:10,000 --> 00:49:11,779
and recursively all the way down.

980
00:49:11,779 --> 00:49:17,680
This is something called the binary search tree property,

981
00:49:17,680 --> 00:49:20,080
BST property.

982
00:49:20,080 --> 00:49:23,540
Here we're calling them binary tree sets,

983
00:49:23,540 --> 00:49:25,220
or set binary trees.

984
00:49:25,220 --> 00:49:26,879
But they're also known in the literature

985
00:49:26,879 --> 00:49:29,500
as binary search trees, a term you may have heard before.

986
00:49:29,500 --> 00:49:30,859
So this is a special case of what

987
00:49:30,859 --> 00:49:33,600
we're doing where we're storing the keys in order.

988
00:49:33,600 --> 00:49:37,919
And then if I want to search for a key like 13,

989
00:49:37,919 --> 00:49:39,819
I compare that key with the root.

990
00:49:39,819 --> 00:49:43,100
I see, oh, it's not equal, and it's to the left

991
00:49:43,100 --> 00:49:44,799
because it's less than 17.

992
00:49:44,799 --> 00:49:46,919
So 13 is left of here.

993
00:49:46,919 --> 00:49:48,700
13 is right of 7.

994
00:49:48,700 --> 00:49:50,359
13 is right of 12.

995
00:49:50,359 --> 00:49:55,060
And so I know that this is where 13 would belong, but there's no

996
00:49:55,060 --> 00:49:55,740
right child there.

997
00:49:55,740 --> 00:49:58,740
And so I know in find, I just return nothing.

998
00:49:58,740 --> 00:50:03,640
If I was doing find previous, I would return this node

999
00:50:03,640 --> 00:50:05,920
because I have tried to go to the right.

1000
00:50:05,920 --> 00:50:08,360
The last time before I fell off the tree,

1001
00:50:08,360 --> 00:50:09,740
I was trying to go to the right.

1002
00:50:09,740 --> 00:50:12,860
And therefore, that last node I had was the previous item.

1003
00:50:12,860 --> 00:50:15,340
If I was trying to do find next, what would I do?

1004
00:50:15,340 --> 00:50:18,600
I would just take this node and compute its successor, which

1005
00:50:18,600 --> 00:50:19,860
we already know how to do.

1006
00:50:19,860 --> 00:50:22,120
And that happens to be the root.

1007
00:50:22,120 --> 00:50:24,640
So now I can do these inexact searches.

1008
00:50:24,640 --> 00:50:27,940
When I do find previous and find next, when I fall off the tree,

1009
00:50:27,940 --> 00:50:30,020
I find either the previous or the next.

1010
00:50:30,020 --> 00:50:31,680
And then with predecessor or successor,

1011
00:50:31,680 --> 00:50:33,420
I can find the other one.

1012
00:50:33,420 --> 00:50:41,100
So that's how we can do find and find previous and find next.

1013
00:50:41,100 --> 00:50:47,240
To do sequences, we need a little bit more work.

1014
00:50:47,240 --> 00:50:50,200
We'll do that next time.

1015
00:50:54,640 --> 00:50:55,640
Thank you.

{"content": "#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Merge word-by-word SRT into sentences + generate bilingual (EN+CN).
Handles: 10-7 AVL Trees (fragmented), 12-8 Binary Heaps (normal).
Output: D:\b站视频\解析视频\【MIT6.006最新】算法导论(中英2020春) Introduction to Algorithms 麻省理工\字幕文件
"""
import re, os, math

OUT_DIR = r'D:\b站视频\解析视频\【MIT6.006最新】算法导论(中英2020春) Introduction to Algorithms 麻省理工\字幕文件'

def parse_srt(path):
    """Parse SRT into list of (index, start_ms, end_ms, text)."""
    with open(path, 'r', encoding='utf-8') as f:
        raw = f.read()
    blocks = re.split(r'\n\n+', raw.strip())
    entries = []
    for blk in blocks:
        lines = blk.strip().split('\n')
        if len(lines) < 3:
            continue
        idx = lines[0]
        ts = lines[1]
        text = '\n'.join(lines[2:])
        # Parse timestamp
        m = re.match(r'(\d+):(\d+):(\d+)[,.](\d+)\s*-->\s*(\d+):(\d+):(\d+)[,.](\d+)', ts)
        if not m:
            continue
        start = int(m.group(1))*3600000 + int(m.group(2))*60000 + int(m.group(3))*1000 + int(m.group(4))
        end   = int(m.group(5))*3600000 + int(m.group(6))*60000 + int(m.group(7))*1000 + int(m.group(8))
        entries.append((int(idx), start, end, text.strip()))
    return entries

def time_to_srt(ms):
    """Convert ms to SRT timestamp format."""
    h = ms // 3600000
    ms -= h * 3600000
    m = ms // 60000
    ms -= m * 60000
    s = ms // 1000
    ms_ = ms % 1000
    return f'{h:02d}:{m:02d}:{s:02d},{ms_:03d}'

def should_merge_gap(e1, e2, max_gap_ms=800):
    """Should two consecutive entries be merged based on time gap?"""
    gap = e2[1] - e1[2]  # e2 start - e1 end
    return gap <= max_gap_ms and gap >= -2000  # allow slight overlap

def merge_entries(entries, max_gap_ms=800):
    """Merge consecutive short entries into groups. Returns list of (start, end, text)."""
    if not entries:
        return []
    merged = []
    group_start = entries[0][1]
    group_end = entries[0][2]
    group_texts = [entries[0][3]]
    
    for i in range(1, len(entries)):
        prev = entries[i-1]
        curr = entries[i]
        
        # Check if should merge
        gap = curr[1] - prev[2]
        curr_text = curr[3].strip()
        
        # Always merge unless:
        # 1. Big time gap (>800ms) AND
        # 2. Current entry ends with sentence-ending punctuation OR
        # 3. Current entry is long (> ~50 chars)
        is_end_of_sentence = any(curr_text.endswith(p) for p in '.!?:;')
        is_long = len(curr_text) > 40
        big_gap = gap > max_gap_ms
        
        if big_gap and (is_end_of_sentence or is_long):
            # Finalize current group
            merged.append((group_start, group_end, ' '.join(group_texts)))
            group_start = curr[1]
            group_end = curr[2]
            group_texts = [curr_text]
        else:
            # Merge: extend group
            if curr_text:
                # Add space if previous text didn't end with one
                if group_texts and not group_texts[-1].endswith(' '):
                    group_texts.append(' ' + curr_text)
                else:
                    group_texts.append(curr_text)
            group_end = curr[2]
    
    # Last group

{"content": "#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Generate bilingual SRT for:
  10-7. Binary Trees Part 2 (AVL)  — word-by-word → merge into clean subs
  12-8. Binary Heaps                — normal paragraphs → direct translate

import re, os

os.makedirs(OUT_DIR, exist_ok=True)

def parse_srt(path):
    with open(path, 'r', encoding='utf-8') as f:
        raw = f.read()
    blocks = re.split(r'\n\n+', raw.strip())
    entries = []
    for blk in blocks:
        lines = blk.strip().split('\n')
        if len(lines) < 3: continue
        idx, ts = lines[0], lines[1]
        text = '\n'.join(lines[2:]).strip()
        m = re.match(r'(\d+):(\d+):(\d+)[,.](\d+)\s*-->\s*(\d+):(\d+):(\d+)[,.](\d+)', ts)
        if not m: continue
        start = int(m[1])*3600000 + int(m[2])*60000 + int(m[3])*1000 + int(m[4])
        end   = int(m[5])*3600000 + int(m[6])*60000 + int(m[7])*1000 + int(m[8])
        entries.append((int(idx), start, end, text))
    return entries

def ts_ms(ms):
    h = ms // 3600000; ms %= 3600000
    m = ms // 60000; ms %= 60000
    s = ms // 1000; f = ms % 1000
    return f'{h:02d}:{m:02d}:{s:02d},{f:03d}'

def clean_text(text):
    # Remove repeated adjacent dupes from bad transcription
    words = re.split(r'(\s+)', text)
    cleaned = []
    prev = None
    for w in words:
        if w.strip():
            if w.strip().lower() != (prev or '').lower():
                cleaned.append(w)
                prev = w.strip()
        else:
            if not cleaned or cleaned[-1] != w:
                cleaned.append(w)
    text = ''.join(cleaned)
    # Space before punctuation
    text = re.sub(r'\s+([.,!?:;)])', r'\1', text)
    text = re.sub(r'\s{2,}', ' ', text).strip()
    return text

def merge_avl(entries):
    """Merge word-by-word AVL entries into readable subtitles."""
    MAX_DUR_MS = 10000   # max 10 sec per subtitle
    MAX_CHARS   = 300     # max 300 chars per subtitle
    MIN_GAP_MS  = 350     # gap threshold for sentence boundary
    
    # Phase 1: group by time proximity
    groups = []
    cur = [entries[0]]
    for e in entries[1:]:
        gap = e[1] - cur[-1][2]
        dur = e[1] - cur[0][1]
        
        text_so_far = ' '.join(c[3] for c in cur)
        
        # Split on: big gap + (period or long text or long duration)
        is_end = (gap > MIN_GAP_MS and any(c[3].rstrip().endswith(('.','!','?')) for c in cur[-3:]))
        too_big = gap > 2000
        too_long = len(text_so_far) > MAX_CHARS
        too_long_dur = dur > MAX_DUR_MS
        
        if (too_big or (is_end and (too_long or too_long_dur))):
            groups.append(cur)
            cur = [e]
        else:
            cur.append(e)
    if cur:
        groups.append(cur)
    
    # Phase 2: combine text per group
    merged = []
    for g in groups:
        text = ' '.join(e[3] for e in g)
        text = clean_text(text)
        if text:
            merged.append((g[0][1], g[-1][2], text))
    return merged

# =====================================================================
# Heaps (12-8): normal paragraphs -> write EN base + translation stubs
# =====================================================================
def process_heaps():
    src = r'网络共享文件夹/12-8. Binary Heaps-720P 准高清-AVC.realcugan (transcribed on 23-May-2026 18-34-58).srt'
    out = os.path.join(OUT_DIR, '12-8_Binary_Heaps_双语.srt')
    
    entries = parse_srt(src)
    print(f'Heaps: {len(entries)} entries')
    
    with open(out, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
        for idx, start, end, text in entries:
            text = clean_text(text)
            f.write(f'{idx}\n{ts_ms(start)} --> {ts_ms(end)}\n{text}\n\n')
    
    filesize = os.path.getsize(out)
    print(f'  -> {out} ({filesize:,} bytes)')
    return entries

# =====================================================================
# AVL (10-7): word-by-word -> merge -> EN base
# =====================================================================
def process_avl():
    src = r'网络共享文件夹/10-7. Binary Trees, Part 2 AVL-720P 准高清-AVC.realcugan (transcribed on 25-May-2026 11-28-47).srt'
    out = os.path.join(OUT_DIR, '10-7_Binary_Trees_Part2_AVL_双语.srt')
    
    entries = parse_srt(src)
    print(f'AVL: {len(entries)} raw entries')
    
    merged = merge_avl(entries)
    print(f'AVL: merged into {len(merged)} groups')
    
    with open(out, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
        for i, (start, end, text) in enumerate(merged, 1):
            f.write(f'{i}\n{ts_ms(start)} --> {ts_ms(end)}\n{text}\n\n')
    
    filesize = os.path.getsize(out)
    print(f'  -> {out} ({filesize:,} bytes)')
    return merged

# Run
print('='*60)

print()

print(f'\nDone. Output files are EN-only. Next step: add Chinese translations.')
print(f'Heaps: {len(heaps)} entries')
print(f'AVL:   {len(avl)} entries')

# Write update function
def update_file(filename, add_dict):
    path = os.path.join(OUT_DIR, filename)
    with open(path, 'r', encoding='utf-8') as f:
        raw = f.read()
    blocks = re.split(r'\n\n+', raw.strip())
    
    out_lines = []
    t_added = 0
    for blk in blocks:
        lines = blk.strip().split('\n')
        if len(lines) < 3:
            continue
        idx = lines[0]
        ts = lines[1]
        en_text = '\n'.join(lines[2:])
        out_lines.append(idx)
        out_lines.append(ts)
        out_lines.append(en_text)
        # Check if translation exists
        has_cn = len(lines) >= 4 and lines[3].strip()
        if idx in add_dict and add_dict[idx]:
            out_lines.append(add_dict[idx])
            t_added += 1
        elif has_cn:
            out_lines.append(lines[3])
        out_lines.append('')
    
    with open(path, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
        f.write('\n'.join(out_lines).strip() + '\n')
    
    # Count stats
    total_t = sum(1 for b in re.split(r'\n\n+', open(path, 'r', encoding='utf-8').read().strip()) if len(b.split('\n')) >= 4)
    print(f'  {filename}: +{t_added} added, {total_t} total translated')

def parse_srt(path):
    with open(path, 'r', encoding='utf-8') as f:
        raw = f.read()
    blocks = re.split(r'\n\n+', raw.strip())
    entries = []
    for blk in blocks:
        lines = blk.strip().split('\n')
        if len(lines) < 3: continue
        idx, ts = lines[0], lines[1]
        text = '\n'.join(lines[2:]).strip()
        m = re.match(r'(\d+):(\d+):(\d+)[,.](\d+)\s*-->\s*(\d+):(\d+):(\d+)[,.](\d+)', ts)
        if not m: continue
        start = int(m[1])*3600000 + int(m[2])*60000 + int(m[3])*1000 + int(m[4])
        end   = int(m[5])*3600000 + int(m[6])*60000 + int(m[7])*1000 + int(m[8])
        entries.append((int(idx), start, end, text))
    return entries

def ts_ms(ms):
    h = ms // 3600000; ms %= 3600000
    m = ms // 60000; ms %= 60000
    s = ms // 1000; f = ms % 1000
    return f'{h:02d}:{m:02d}:{s:02d},{f:03d}'

def clean_text(text):
    words = re.split(r'(\s+)', text)
    cleaned = []; prev = None
    for w in words:
        if w.strip():
            if w.strip().lower() != (prev or '').lower():
                cleaned.append(w); prev = w.strip()
        else:
            if not cleaned or cleaned[-1] != w: cleaned.append(w)
    text = ''.join(cleaned)
    text = re.sub(r'\s+([.,!?:;)])', r'\1', text)
    text = re.sub(r'\s{2,}', ' ', text).strip()
    return text

def merge_entries(entries):
    MAX_DUR_MS = 10000; MAX_CHARS = 300; MIN_GAP_MS = 350
    groups = [[entries[0]]]
    for e in entries[1:]:
        gap = e[1] - groups[-1][-1][2]
        dur = e[1] - groups[-1][0][1]
        text_so_far = ' '.join(c[3] for c in groups[-1])
        is_end = (gap > MIN_GAP_MS and any(c[3].rstrip().endswith(('.','!','?')) for c in groups[-1][-3:]))
        too_big = gap > 2000
        too_long = len(text_so_far) > MAX_CHARS
        too_long_dur = dur > MAX_DUR_MS
        if too_big or (is_end and (too_long or too_long_dur)):
            groups.append([e])
        else:
            groups[-1].append(e)
    merged = []
    for g in groups:
        text = clean_text(' '.join(e[3] for e in g))

print(f'EN-only written: {en_path}')

# Now read back and add translations based on ACTUAL content
with open(en_path, 'r', encoding='utf-8') as f:

blocks = re.split(r'\n\n+', raw.strip())

# Build translation dict by reading actual EN text
translations = {}
for blk in blocks:

# Write final output
final_path = en_path
with open(final_path, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
    t_count = 0
    for blk in blocks:
        lines = blk.strip().split('\n')
        if len(lines) < 3: continue
        idx = lines[0]; ts = lines[1]; en = lines[2]
        f.write(f'{idx}\n{ts}\n{en}\n')
        
        # Get translation based on actual EN content
        cn = get_translation(idx, en)
        if cn:
            f.write(f'{cn}\n')
            t_count += 1

    print(f'Final: {t_count} translated out of {len(blocks)} entries')

{"content": "#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Smart merge: word-by-word SRT -> ~1000 short subtitle groups + bilingual."""
import re, os

OUT_DIR = r'D:\b站视频\解析视频\【MIT6.006最新】算法导论(中英2020春) Introduction to Algorithms 麻省理工\字幕文件'
os.makedirs(OUT_DIR, exist_ok=True)

def parse_srt(path):
    with open(path, 'r', encoding='utf-8') as f:
        raw = f.read()
    blocks = re.split(r'\n\n+', raw.strip())
    entries = []
    for blk in blocks:
        lines = blk.strip().split('\n')
        if len(lines) < 3: continue
        ts = lines[1]; text = '\n'.join(lines[2:]).strip()
        m = re.match(r'(\d+):(\d+):(\d+)[,.](\d+)\s*-->\s*(\d+):(\d+):(\d+)[,.](\d+)', ts)
        if not m: continue
        start = int(m[1])*3600000+int(m[2])*60000+int(m[3])*1000+int(m[4])
        end   = int(m[5])*3600000+int(m[6])*60000+int(m[7])*1000+int(m[8])
        entries.append((start, end, text))
    return entries

def ts_ms(ms):
    h=ms//3600000; ms%=3600000; m=ms//60000; ms%=60000; s=ms//1000; f=ms%1000
    return f'{h:02d}:{m:02d}:{s:02d},{f:03d}'

def clean_text(text):
    words = re.split(r'(\s+)', text); cleaned = []; prev = None
    for w in words:
        if w.strip():
            if w.strip().lower() != (prev or '').lower():
                cleaned.append(w); prev = w.strip()
        else:
            if not cleaned or cleaned[-1] != w: cleaned.append(w)
    text = ''.join(cleaned)
    text = re.sub(r'\s+([.,!?:;)])', r'\1', text)
    text = re.sub(r'\s{2,}', ' ', text).strip()
    if text and not text[-1] in '.!?':
        text += '.'
    return text

def smart_merge(entries, target_count=1000, max_chars=160, max_dur_ms=8000):
    """Merge word-by-word entries targeting ~target_count groups."""
    if not entries: return []
    
    # Calculate desired merge size
    merge_size = max(1, len(entries) // target_count)
    
    groups = [[entries[0]]]
    for e in entries[1:]:
        gap = e[0] - groups[-1][-1][1]
        dur = e[0] - groups[-1][0][0]
        text_so_far = ' '.join(c[2] for c in groups[-1])
        too_long = len(text_so_far) > max_chars
        too_long_dur = dur > max_dur_ms
        big_gap = gap > 500
        
        # Split on: big gap + sentence end, OR too long text, OR too long duration
        # Also split if we've merged enough words
        word_count = len(text_so_far.split())
        enough_words = word_count >= merge_size
        
        if (big_gap and text_so_far.rstrip().endswith(('.','!','?'))) or too_long or too_long_dur or (enough_words and big_gap):
            groups.append([e])
        else:
            groups[-1].append(e)
    
    # Finalize
    merged = []
    for g in groups:
        text = clean_text(' '.join(e[2] for e in g))
        if text:
            merged.append((g[0][0], g[-1][1], text))
    return merged

def write_bilingual(entries, path, trans_dict):
    with open(path, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
        t, ut = 0, 0
        for i, (start, end, text) in enumerate(entries, 1):
            f.write(f'{i}\n{ts_ms(start)} --> {ts_ms(end)}\n{text}\n')
            if str(i) in trans_dict and trans_dict[str(i)]:
                f.write(trans_dict[str(i)] + '\n')
                t += 1
            else:
                ut += 1
            f.write('\n')
    print(f'  {os.path.basename(path)}: {t} translated, {ut} EN-only')
    return t

# =====================================================================
# Process AVL (10-7)
# =====================================================================
avl_src = r'网络共享文件夹/10-7. Binary Trees, Part 2 AVL-720P 准高清-AVC.realcugan (transcribed on 25-May-2026 11-28-47).srt'
avl_dst = os.path.join(OUT_DIR, '10-7_Binary_Trees_Part2_AVL_双语.srt')

raw = parse_srt(avl_src)
print(f'AVL: {len(raw)} raw entries')
merged = smart_merge(raw, target_count=1000, max_chars=160, max_dur_ms=8000)
print(f'AVL: merged into {len(merged)} groups')

# Write bilingual
write_bilingual(merged, avl_dst, {})

# =====================================================================
# Process Problem Session 4 (11)
# =====================================================================
ps_src = r'网络共享文件夹/11-Problem Session 4-720P 准高清-AVC.realcugan.2 (transcribed on 23-May-2026 22-03-36).srt'
ps_dst = os.path.join(OUT_DIR, '11-Problem_Session_4_双语.srt')

raw2 = parse_srt(ps_src)
print(f'\nProblem Session: {len(raw2)} raw entries')
merged2 = smart_merge(raw2, target_count=1000, max_chars=160, max_dur_ms=8000)
print(f'Problem Session: merged into {len(merged2)} groups')

# Write bilingual
write_bilingual(merged2, ps_dst, {})

print(f'\nOutput directory: {OUT_DIR}')
", "path": "merge_all.py"}

"""Propagate v2 translations to v3 entries by matching EN text overlap."""
import re, os

def read_entries(path):
    with open(path, 'r', encoding='utf-8') as f:
        raw = f.read()
    blocks = re.split(r'\n\n+', raw.strip())
    entries = []
    for blk in blocks:
        lines = blk.strip().split('\n')
        if len(lines) < 3: continue
        idx = lines[0]; ts = lines[1]; en = lines[2]
        cn = lines[3] if len(lines) >= 4 and lines[3].strip() else None
        entries.append((idx, ts, en, cn))
    return entries

# Load v2: each entry has EN and possibly CN
v2 = read_entries(v2_path)

for i, (idx3, ts3, en3, _) in enumerate(v3):
    en3_clean = en3.strip()
    best_match = None
    best_overlap = 0
    
    for idx2, ts2, en2, cn2 in v2:
        if not cn2: continue
        # Check how much of v3's EN appears in v2's EN
        en2_clean = en2.strip()
        # Count overlapping words
        words3 = set(en3_clean.lower().split())
        words2 = set(en2_clean.lower().split())
        overlap = len(words3 & words2)
        ratio = overlap / len(words3) if words3 else 0
        
        if ratio >= 0.5 and overlap > best_overlap:
            best_overlap = overlap
            best_match = cn2
    
    if best_match:
        translations[idx3] = best_match

print(f'Matched: {len(translations)} entries')

# Write v3 bilingual
with open(out_path, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
    for idx3, ts3, en3, _ in v3:
        f.write(f'{idx3}\n{ts3}\n{en3}\n')
        if idx3 in translations:
            f.write(translations[idx3] + '\n')
        f.write('\n')

print(f'Written: {out_path}')
print(f'Translated: {len(translations)}/{len(v3)}')
print(f'File size: {os.path.getsize(out_path):,} bytes')
